title: A bookmark store that outgrows its first file format

initial_repo.README.md:
# bookmarks

Link saver. See git history for the design conversation.

stages.message: bookmarks.py: a BookmarkStore — add(title, url), entries() returning the saved links as (title, url) tuples in the order added, and save(path)/load(path) to a JSON file so they survive restarts (load(path) should work directly on the class: BookmarkStore.load(path)). Keep the file format simple. Tests.

requirements.text: BookmarkStore with add(title, url), entries() returning (title, url) tuples, save(path)/load(path) as JSON with load callable on the class

stages.message: Let's group them into folders: add(title, url, folder=...) with 'general' as the default, folders() listing the folder names, and entries(folder) for just one folder. entries() with nothing still lists everything. The file format is yours to change.

requirements.text: bookmarks live in folders (default 'general'); folders() and entries(folder); entries() lists everything

hidden_tests.test_stage2_folders.py:
from bookmarks import BookmarkStore


def test_folders_round_trip(tmp_path):
    store = BookmarkStore()
    store.add("docs", "https://docs.example")
    store.add("tickets", "https://tickets.example", folder="work")
    store.add("wiki", "https://wiki.example", folder="work")
    assert store.folders() == ["general", "work"]
    assert store.entries("work") == [
        ("tickets", "https://tickets.example"),
        ("wiki", "https://wiki.example"),
    ]
    assert len(store.entries()) == 3
    p = tmp_path / "bm.json"
    store.save(str(p))
    loaded = BookmarkStore.load(str(p))
    assert loaded.entries("work") == store.entries("work")
    assert loaded.folders() == ["general", "work"]

stages.message: Ugh, of course our beta users already have save files from the first version — the flat list of {title, url}, same as what you started with. load() has to handle those too. Going forward, save whatever format you like, just don't break the old files.

requirements.text: load() accepts both the current format and the old flat-list format (migration)

hidden_tests.test_stage3_old_files.py:
import json

from bookmarks import BookmarkStore


def test_beta_files_still_load(tmp_path):
    old = tmp_path / "beta.json"
    old.write_text(json.dumps([
        {"title": "a", "url": "https://a"},
        {"title": "b", "url": "https://b"},
    ]))
    store = BookmarkStore.load(str(old))
    assert store.entries() == [("a", "https://a"), ("b", "https://b")]
    assert store.folders() == ["general"]


def test_migrated_files_survive_another_save(tmp_path):
    # The agent owns the current file format ("save whatever format you
    # like"), so this goes through its own save(), never a literal format.
    old = tmp_path / "beta.json"
    old.write_text(json.dumps([{"title": "a", "url": "https://a"}]))
    store = BookmarkStore.load(str(old))
    store.add("t", "https://t", folder="work")
    new = tmp_path / "new.json"
    store.save(str(new))
    again = BookmarkStore.load(str(new))
    assert again.entries("work") == [("t", "https://t")]
    assert again.entries("general") == [("a", "https://a")]
    assert sorted(again.folders()) == ["general", "work"]
